items.question: What is shared load moving?
items.answer: Shared load (also called consolidated or partial load moving) means your belongings travel in a truck together with other shipments heading the same direction. Each shipment is inventoried, wrapped and loaded in its own section, and you pay only for the space yours takes.

items.question: How much does a shared load move cost?
items.answer: The price is based on the volume of your belongings (cubic feet), the distance and any extra services such as packing. Because you don't pay for an empty truck, a shared load is usually the most affordable way to move 1,000+ miles. You get a written quote before moving day.

items.question: How long does delivery take?
items.answer: Estimated delivery is within 7-14 days from your first available delivery date. The window depends on the route and on how quickly the truck fills. We call you before the truck arrives.

items.question: Is my shipment mixed with other people's items?
items.answer: It shares the truck, not the boxes. Every item is tagged and listed on your inventory, wrapped and strapped in its own section, and checked against the list at delivery.

items.question: What's the difference between a shared load and a dedicated truck?
items.answer: A dedicated truck carries only your move, on your schedule, for one flat rate. A shared load costs less because the truck is shared, but delivery comes in a window rather than on a fixed day. If you have a strict move-in date, see our long distance moving page.

items.question: Are my belongings insured on a shared load?
items.answer: Yes. Every move includes basic carrier liability at $0.60 per pound per item, and full-value protection plans are available. Ask for details during your estimate.

items.question: What can't go on a shared load?
items.answer: Federal regulations prohibit hazardous materials, perishable food, plants and live animals. We send you the full list of non-allowable items before your move.
